title: Practice extracts: The Lens, The Owl and The 7:12
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lesson 52 (Practice extracts 'The Lens', 'The Owl' and 'The 7:12' (teacher-written, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 52: Structure: how ideas develop across a whole text. Teacher-written for TGA. Read, then answer under time.

passage.title: The Lens
paras: The lighthouse keeper's cottage is a museum now. You pay at a little window and climb the same hundred and twelve steps he climbed each night, though nobody makes you do it in a gale. At the top, behind glass, sits the great lens: a beehive of prisms taller than a man, so clean it seems to hold the sky. A card explains how it turned on a bath of mercury, so smoothly that a child could push it. I did push it, very gently, when the guide was not looking. It moved. Somewhere, two hundred years of ships seemed to move with it.

passage.title: The Owl
paras: We had been told the owl would come at dusk, so we came at four and waited. The barn smelled of dust and old hay. My brother whispered about football until I glared at him. Then, without a sound, a white shape slid out of the dark beam above us, turned its flat moon of a face towards the field, and was gone. That was all. Ten seconds, perhaps. We walked home without speaking, as if we had been in a mosque, and my brother, who never stops talking, did not say a word until the gate.

passage.title: The 7:12
paras: Every weekday I spend fifty minutes on the 7:12. Most people treat it as dead time: phones, headphones, eyes shut. I used to. Then, one grey March, the signal failed for an hour outside a village I had passed five hundred times and never seen. A woman across the aisle offered me half her orange. A student read us the funny bits of his textbook. By the time the train moved, the carriage was a small, temporary town. It has never happened again. But now I look up from my phone, just in case.

questions.q: Track 'The Lens' with the four-step tracker
questions.a: Opening: the museum and ticket window; shift: the climb and the lens; turning point: 'I did push it'; ending: the ships of two hundred years.

questions.q: Name the tense shift in 'The 7:12' and its effect
questions.a: present to past and back to present: routine, the special day, a changed routine.
